name: Astrophysics
description: The application of physics to understand celestial objects and phenomena.

name: Cosmology
description: The study of the origin, evolution, and large-scale structure of the universe.

name: Planetary Science
description: The study of planets, moons, and planetary systems.

name: Stellar Astronomy
description: The study of stars, their structure, evolution, and populations.

name: Galactic Astronomy
description: The study of galaxies and their structure, dynamics, and evolution.

name: Observational Astronomy
description: The practice of observing and measuring celestial objects across the electromagnetic spectrum.

name: Astrometry
description: The precise measurement of the positions and motions of celestial bodies.

name: Solar Physics
description: The study of the Sun, its structure, activity, and influence.

name: Astrobiology
description: The study of the origin, evolution, and distribution of life in the universe.

name: Astrochemistry
description: The study of chemical processes and molecules in space.

name: Astrology
description: The historical and cultural system attributing earthly events to celestial positions, now regarded as a non-scientific practice.

name: Stellar Astrophysics
description: The physical study of stellar interiors, atmospheres, and evolution.

name: Plasma Astrophysics
description: The study of astrophysical plasmas and their magnetic behavior.

name: High-Energy Astrophysics
description: The study of the most energetic phenomena in the universe.

name: X-Ray Astronomy
description: Observation of celestial X-ray sources such as black holes and supernova remnants.

name: Gamma-Ray Astronomy
description: Observation of the highest-energy photons from cosmic sources.

name: Relativistic Astrophysics
description: The study of phenomena governed by general relativity, such as black holes and gravitational waves.

name: Particle Astrophysics
description: The study of elementary particles of cosmic origin, including cosmic rays and neutrinos.

name: Computational Astrophysics
description: Numerical simulation and modeling of astrophysical systems.

name: Nuclear Astrophysics
description: The study of nuclear reactions in stars and their role in element synthesis.

name: Accretion Physics
description: The study of how matter falls onto compact objects, powering disks and jets.

name: Physical Cosmology
description: The physical theory of the universe's origin and evolution.

name: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
description: The production of light elements in the first minutes after the Big Bang.

name: Cosmic Microwave Background
description: The relic radiation from the early universe used to constrain cosmological parameters.

name: Structure Formation
description: The growth of galaxies and large-scale structure from primordial density fluctuations.

name: Dark Matter
description: The study of the unseen mass whose gravity shapes galaxies and clusters.

name: Dark Energy
description: The study of the unknown energy driving the accelerating expansion of the universe.

name: Inflationary Cosmology
description: The theory of a rapid exponential expansion in the very early universe.

name: Observational Cosmology
description: The measurement of the universe's expansion, structure, and content through observation.

name: Theoretical Cosmology
description: The mathematical modeling of the universe's evolution and geometry.

name: Gravitational Lensing
description: The bending of light by mass, used to map dark matter and study distant galaxies.

name: Planetology
description: The comparative study of planets and their properties.

name: Exoplanet Science
description: The detection and characterization of planets orbiting other stars.

name: Lunar Science
description: The study of the Moon, its origin, geology, and resources.

name: Planetary Atmospheres
description: The study of the atmospheres of planets and their evolution.

name: Small Body Science
description: The study of asteroids, comets, and meteoroids.

name: Asteroid Science
description: The study of asteroids, their composition, and dynamics.

name: Comet Science
description: The study of comets and their nuclei, comae, and tails.

name: Meteoritics
description: The study of meteorites and their parent bodies.

name: Planetary Habitability
description: The study of conditions under which planets can support life.

name: Stellar Structure
description: The physical modeling of stellar interiors and energy transport.

name: Stellar Evolution
description: The life cycles of stars from formation to death.

name: Stellar Nucleosynthesis
description: The synthesis of chemical elements inside stars.

name: Variable Stars
description: The study of stars whose brightness changes over time.

name: Binary Stars
description: The study of star systems with two gravitationally bound members.

name: Star Formation
description: The processes by which stars form from collapsing molecular clouds.

name: Compact Objects
description: The study of dense stellar remnants and black holes.

name: White Dwarfs
description: The study of degenerate remnants of low-mass stars.

name: Neutron Stars
description: The study of ultra-dense neutron-rich stellar remnants, including pulsars.

name: Black Holes
description: The study of regions of spacetime where gravity prevents all escape.

name: Supernovae
description: The study of explosive stellar deaths and their remnants.

name: Brown Dwarfs
description: The study of substellar objects too small to sustain hydrogen fusion.

name: Galactic Structure
description: The study of the components and morphology of galaxies.

name: Galactic Dynamics
description: The study of the gravitational motion of stars and gas within galaxies.

name: Galaxy Formation and Evolution
description: The study of how galaxies form, grow, and change over cosmic time.

name: Active Galactic Nuclei
description: The study of supermassive black holes powering luminous galactic cores and quasars.

name: Interstellar Medium
description: The study of gas and dust between stars and the birth of new stars within it.

name: Star Clusters
description: The study of gravitationally bound groups of stars.

name: Galactic Archaeology
description: The reconstruction of galaxy formation history from stellar populations.

name: Optical Astronomy
description: Observation of the universe in visible light.

name: Infrared Astronomy
description: Observation of cool objects and dust-enshrouded regions in infrared light.

name: Ultraviolet Astronomy
description: Observation of hot stars and interstellar gas in ultraviolet light.

name: Radio Astronomy
description: Observation of the universe at radio wavelengths, including cold gas and pulsars.

name: Submillimeter Astronomy
description: Observation at submillimeter wavelengths to study star-forming regions and distant galaxies.

name: Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
description: The detection of ripples in spacetime from merging compact objects.

name: Multi-Messenger Astronomy
description: The coordinated study of cosmic events through photons, neutrinos, and gravitational waves.

name: Time-Domain Astronomy
description: The study of objects whose brightness or position changes over time.

name: Positional Astronomy
description: The measurement of celestial coordinates and apparent motions.

name: Celestial Mechanics
description: The gravitational theory of the motions of celestial bodies.

name: Celestial Reference Systems
description: The definition of coordinate frames and standards for celestial positions.

name: Helioseismology
description: The study of solar internal structure through its oscillations.

name: Solar Activity
description: The study of sunspots, flares, and the solar cycle.

name: Solar Wind
description: The study of the stream of charged particles flowing from the Sun.

name: Solar Magnetohydrodynamics
description: The study of the Sun's magnetized plasma dynamics.

name: Exobiology
description: The study of the possibility and forms of life beyond Earth.

name: Biosignatures
description: The search for observable indicators of past or present life.

name: Origin of Life
description: The study of how life arose from non-living matter.

name: Prebiotic Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the processes that may have led to the first biomolecules.

name: Interstellar Chemistry
description: The study of chemical reactions and molecules in interstellar space.
